question: What term describes the natural habitat where a pathogen lives and multiplies?
explanation: A reservoir serves as the primary home and source where pathogens survive and reproduce before moving to a new host. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why must nurses understand all links in the chain of infection?

options.A: To effectively break the cycle and prevent disease spread
options.B: To determine the financial cost of hospital admissions
options.C: To accurately diagnose the specific strain of bacteria
options.D: To calculate the exact incubation period for every patient

explanation: Interrupting any single link in the chain stops the transmission of infectious agents to vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h1)

question: A non-living surrounding that supports the survival of a pathogen is called what?
explanation: Soil, water, and food act as non-living environmental reservoirs where certain pathogens thrive. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why is identifying the reservoir critical for disease control?

options.A: It targets the primary source where pathogens live and multiply
options.B: It guarantees immediate immunity for all exposed hospital staff
options.C: It shortens the standard antibiotic treatment duration for patients
options.D: It eliminates the need for standard hand hygiene practices

explanation: Directing control measures at the source of the pathogen prevents further spread into the community or ward. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is an individual called who harbors a pathogen without ever showing symptoms?
explanation: Asymptomatic carriers spread infections unknowingly because they appear completely healthy while shedding the pathogen. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h3)

question: A patient recovering from typhoid fever continues to shed bacteria in stool samples. What type of human reservoir is this?
explanation: Convalescent carriers shed infectious agents during the recovery phase after their acute symptoms have disappeared. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is an infectious disease that is transmissible from animals to humans called?
explanation: Zoonotic diseases naturally pass between vertebrate animals and human populations. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why do animal reservoirs pose a unique challenge for public health eradication efforts?

options.A: Wild animal populations are difficult to isolate, vaccinate, or monitor
options.B: Animals always show severe symptoms when they carry dangerous human pathogens
options.C: Zoonotic pathogens never survive outside an animal host for more than an hour
options.D: Livestock are immune to all forms of bacterial and viral infections

explanation: Controlling disease in wild animal reservoirs is practically impossible compared to treating infected human populations. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which bacterium found commonly in soil causes tetanus after entering a puncture wound?
explanation: Clostridium tetani spores live in soil and dust, entering the body through broken skin barriers. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h5)

question: A patient steps on a rusty nail in a farm field. Which environmental reservoir is the primary source of the risk?
explanation: Soil is the natural environmental reservoir for tetanus spores found frequently around farms and rusty metal outdoors. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is an inanimate object like a contaminated thermometer or bed rail called?
explanation: Fomites are non-living objects that transfer pathogens between patients if disinfection protocols are missed. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h6)

question: A mosquito transmits the malaria parasite from one person to another. What role does the mosquito play?
explanation: Arthropods like mosquitoes act as biological vectors carrying parasites between human hosts. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is proper disinfection of medical equipment crucial in ward management?

options.A: It eliminates the need for nurses to wear sterile gloves
options.B: It transforms airborne pathogens into harmless water droplets
options.C: It prevents inanimate objects from acting as fomite reservoirs
options.D: It permanently cures chronic infections in human carriers

explanation: Cleaning and disinfecting equipment removes pathogens that otherwise colonize surfaces and spread to patients. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h7)

question: Which nursing action directly targets human reservoirs to prevent hospital outbreaks?

options.A: Sprinkling chemical disinfectants across public walkways
options.B: Placing infected patients in appropriate isolation precautions
options.C: Leaving medical waste uncovered in patient hallways
options.D: Stopping all routine handwashing procedures on the ward

explanation: Isolation precautions contain infectious agents within known human cases to protect others on the ward. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h7)
